STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens (romaine/iceberg-type lettuce) with some cut bell pepper strips (red and yellow/green), a few kidney beans, and a couple of yellow pieces that look like cheese or corn-free fried/egg-like chunks (most likely cheese or croutons).

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 484 cm² (treating it as a near-dinner-size plate; I'll use ~480 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Leafy greens (romaine/lettuce)
- Red and yellow bell pepper strips
- Kidney beans (about 4-5 pieces)
- Yellow cubes (cheese or similar)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate):
- Leafy greens: ~30% (145 cm²)
- Bell pepper strips: ~8% (38 cm²)
- Kidney beans: ~2% (10 cm²)
- Yellow cubes: ~4% (19 cm²)
Total covered ≈ 44%, plausible for a small salad on a large plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x height, outer envelope):
- Leafy greens: 145 cm² x 3 cm ≈ 435 ml
- Bell pepper: 38 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 57 ml
- Kidney beans: 10 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 15 ml
- Yellow cubes: 19 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 29 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Leafy greens: 435 x 0.15 ≈ 65 g
- Bell pepper: 57 x 0.6 ≈ 34 g
- Kidney beans: 15 x 0.8 ≈ 12 g (cooked beans are dense)
- Yellow cubes (cheese): 29 x 0.95 ≈ 28 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Leafy greens: 65 g x 17 kcal/100 g ≈ 11 kcal
- Bell pepper: 34 g x 26 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal
- Kidney beans: 12 g x 127 kcal/100 g ≈ 15 kcal
- Cheese: 28 g x 350 kcal/100 g ≈ 98 kcal
Total ≈ 139 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 139 g, 139 kcal. For a visible small side salad covering under half a large plate with no visible dressing, this is plausible.
